1.why: 5/6, 1/24 and 11/24 all live in 24ths while 1/11 is off-family; among the 24ths the two simple values (5/6, 1/24) read as partial-step outputs and 11/24 is the only non-trivial combined numerator.

2.why: Perfectly symmetric set (+/-2, +/-1/2): every option is a sign or reciprocal image of another, so nothing is distinguishable.

3.why: Three powers of ten form a self-generating family and 650000 is off-shape, but which power is the key cannot be recovered from the set.

4.why: 12/-12 is a sign pair and 2/-4 are unrelated; no value is privileged.

5.why: 9, 15, 21 form an arithmetic run of step 6 with 2 as an off-scale outlier; 15 is the median of the run.

6.why: 8, 10, 12, 14 is a complete even run with no median and no derived value.

7.why: 400, 450, 360 cluster and 150 is small, but no arithmetic relation singles one out.

8.why: 34, 36, 38 is a step-2 run around 36 with 16 as an off-scale outlier; the key is the centre the distractors were generated around.

9.why: All four are pi multiples (100pi, 150pi, 250pi, 125pi) and 392.5 is the only value carrying a decimal.

10.why: 28 is exactly 2x14, the classic doubled-distractor relation, so 14 is the generator; 15 and 11 are off-by-one/near noise.

11.why: 12, 36, 108 is a x3 geometric run with 16 off-family; 36 is the centre of the run.

12.why: 2.5 is the only value carrying a decimal (5, 8, 16 are integers) and 5 is its double.

13.why: All four are multiples of 7 (5, 9, 15, 18 x7) with two doubling pairs; no single value is privileged.

14.why: 730, 450, 530, 820 share no ratio, difference or rounding relation.

15.why: 22 and 44 are 2x and 4x of 11, so the three are one linear family; 121 is the lone perfect square and the only value off that family.

16.why: Four weekday names with no numeric or ordering structure to exploit.

17.why: 2, 3, 4, 5 is a complete consecutive run with no median and no outlier.

18.why: 12.5 is the only value carrying a decimal among 24, 20, 18.

19.why: 9, 15, 21 is a step-6 run with 24 off it (and 24 = 9 + 15, a sum-of-two-others distractor); 15 is the median of the run.

20.why: 12.5 is the only value carrying a decimal, and 25 is its double (the doubled-answer distractor).

21.why: 2200, 2420, 2662 is a x1.1 compound chain and 2662 is the only value that is not a round multiple of 100 - the deepest, exactly-computed member of the chain.

22.why: -2/2 is a sign pair and 3, 0 are isolated; nothing privileges one over the pair members.

23.why: 30, 15, 10 are 60/2, 60/4, 60/6 - one family with 11 off it - but which family member is the key is not recoverable.

24.why: 100, 102, 108, 120 are close and share no clean generating relation.

25.why: 54, 60, 66 is a step-6 run with 108 off-scale (= 2x54); 60 is the median of the run.

26.why: 16, 21, 26 is a step-5 run with 22 off it; 21 is the median of the run.

27.why: 7/40 is exactly half of 7/20 and 2/5 = 8/20, so 7/20 is the generator of both; 1/3 is the lone incompatible denominator.

28.why: All four are pi multiples; 904.32 is the only one with hundredths (the others are one-decimal), the lone format outlier.

29.why: 84, 105, 126 are 4, 5, 6 x21 - a step-21 run with 75 off-family - and 105 is its median.

30.why: 11/12 and 17/18 are two adjacent pairs with no derived value or centre.
